## Operating lessons

- **ui-never-settled** (confirmed) — The UI did not publish readable content within the learned budget — screenshot the device before concluding anything about the app.
  - _evidence:_ waited 8s for com.android.settings with no readable dump
- **ios-no-app-data-clear** (seen twice) — iOS cannot clear an app's data from the host: there is no `pm clear` equivalent, so a persisted login survives between runs. Reset through the app's own sign-out flow instead of assuming a clean start.
  - _evidence:_ clear_app_data(com.google.ios.youtube) is unavailable on the iOS adapter
- **blackcode-cli-outdated-v2.3.0** (seen once) — The bk CLI (Blackcode issue tracker integration) installed in this harness is v2.3.0 and is rejected server-side as no longer supported. Any file_issue call fails with: "This bk (v2.3.0) is no longer supported. Update and refresh your agent skill: npm install -g @blackcode_sa/bc-issues@latest ; bk skill install ; bk guide". This is an environment/tooling problem, not a query or finding-id problem — do not retry file_issue with different arguments hoping it's something on the agent side. The fix requires shell access this testing agent does not have (npm install + bk skill install), so it must be done by the user/harness maintainer outside this session. Earlier successful file_issue calls in the same session (before this error started appearing) may still have worked — check_issue_status can confirm whether a previously-filed issue is still reachable even while file_issue itself is broken.
  - _evidence:_ mcp__device__file_issue succeeded earlier in this same session (filed F008 as Blackcode issue #432), then failed on a later call for F005 with the v2.3.0-unsupported error above — same session, same tool, no argument changes that would explain the difference except time passing / a server-side deprecation cutover mid-session.
- **blackcode-cli-utf8-decode** (seen once) — blackcode.py's subprocess.run(bk ..., text=True) without an explicit encoding decodes bk's stdout using locale.getpreferredencoding(), which on Windows is the system codepage (cp1252), not UTF-8. bk emits UTF-8 (issue titles/descriptions are full of em dashes and smart quotes), so a cp1252 decode hit an undefined byte on almost any non-trivial payload -- a subprocess reader-thread crash that left result.stdout as None rather than raising cleanly, so every search_issues/issue_status call failed with an unhelpful AttributeError regardless of query content. Fixed by passing encoding="utf-8" explicitly to subprocess.run in blackcode._run(). If a future subprocess wrapper for another external CLI is added on Windows, give it the same explicit encoding -- text=True alone is not safe for any tool whose output isn't guaranteed ASCII.
  - _evidence:_ search_issues failed on every query (cancel, login, clinic, signup, bug, error, session, empty) with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip' until encoding="utf-8" was added to the subprocess.run call.
- **ios-read-screen-stale-dump-after-system-dialog** (seen once) — On iOS, read_screen can return a stale/wrong dump attributing the screen to a completely unrelated app (observed: com.apple.mobilenotes / Notes, with fixed fake "New Note" content) for one or more calls immediately after a tap that triggers a native iOS system dialog (e.g. "Enable Biometric Login", "Save Password?"). Repeating read_screen does not self-correct reliably — even a second read_screen call after acting on the stale dump can return the exact same stale Notes content again. When this happens, fall back to screenshot + Read-the-image, which reliably shows the true current state (the real dialog or app screen). Once the transient system-dialog sequence fully clears, read_screen resumes returning accurate dumps.
  - _evidence:_ After submitting a correct login on the Metaesthetics doctor iPad app, tapping the LOGIN button and then calling read_screen twice in a row both times returned a dump claiming the screen was owned by com.apple.mobilenotes with static "Notes"/"New Note" content, while a screenshot taken at the same moment showed the real doctor Dashboard underneath an "Enable Biometric Login" system dialog. The same stale-Notes pattern recurred identically on a second, unrelated login attempt later in the same session.
- **record-finding-add-note-param-is-kind** (seen once) — record_finding's verdict-type parameter is named `kind` (values: pass/warning/bug/suggestion), not `type`. add_note's tone parameter is also named `kind` (values include at least pass/bug — not `color`, despite the system prompt describing the note tone as "Green if it passed, amber for a warning or suggestion, red for a bug"). Both tools also require `evidence`/text params up front — calling with the intuitively-named parameter first wastes a turn on an InputValidationError before finding the right name.
  - _evidence:_ In this session, mcp__device__record_finding rejected a call with `type: "pass"` (error: "Additional properties are not allowed ('type' was unexpected)") and only succeeded once the field was renamed to `kind`. Separately, mcp__device__add_note rejected a call with `color: "green"` (error: "'kind' is a required property") and succeeded once `kind: "pass"` was supplied instead.
- **scroll-tool-fixed-middle-band-no-target-position** (seen once) — The `scroll` tool always swipes within the screen's vertical middle band regardless of the `scale` parameter — there is no way to target a specific y-coordinate or a specific horizontally-scrollable widget (e.g. a card carousel) that isn't currently positioned near the middle of the screen. To scroll a horizontal carousel, you'd have to first scroll the page so the carousel lands near vertical center, which is fiddly and costly to get right by trial and error. It's usually far cheaper to test carousel content via its "See all"/expand link and by tapping individual cards by id than to fight the scroll tool into swiping the carousel itself.
  - _evidence:_ On the Metaesthetics app's Home screen, tried to horizontally scroll the "Explore by concern" carousel (positioned around y=1074 out of 2400) using scroll(direction=right/left) and got no effect — the swipe was landing outside the carousel's bounds. Repositioning the carousel toward the middle via several scroll(down/up, scale=X) calls before the horizontal swipe wasted multiple turns and never reliably converged; switching to tapping "See all" and individual cards by id was immediate and gave equivalent coverage.
- **scroll-with-ime-open-triggers-gboard-glide-typing** (seen once) — When a text field is focused and the on-screen keyboard (IME) is showing, calling `scroll` can swipe across the keyboard area itself (scroll always uses the screen's vertical middle band, and the IME can occupy much of the lower half of the screen). That swipe gets interpreted by Gboard as a glide/swipe-type gesture and silently appends stray characters (observed: " G6", twice, reproducibly) to the focused field's text — not an app bug. If you need to scroll a screen that has a focused text input with the keyboard open, dismiss the keyboard first (tap elsewhere / press back once) or scroll before focusing the field, then re-check the field's actual text with read_screen before trusting it.
  - _evidence:_ On the Search screen, typing "Anti-Aging Mesotherapy" into the search box left it reading correctly, but after calling `scroll(down)` while the keyboard was still open, read_screen showed the field text had become "Anti-Aging Mesotherapy G6" with a 'No Results Found' message. Cleared and retyped "Mesotherapy" (clean), scrolled again, and it became "Mesotherapy G6" a second time — reproducible. With the keyboard already dismissed (no scroll needed, results rendered without scrolling), the same search term stayed exactly as typed.
- **wait-until-gone-poisons-record-finding-on-timeout** (seen once) — Do not call wait_until_gone with text that is not an actual transient loading indicator (e.g. static auto-filled form content). If the text never disappears and the call times out, record_finding's freshness guard appears to keep treating that exact string as "loading text still on screen" and refuses to file — even after a fresh read_screen — as long as that string still appears anywhere in the dump. Since the string can be permanent page content, this can become impossible to clear by waiting. Workaround: navigate to a screen where that string is no longer in the DOM (e.g. Cancel out of the form) and read_screen there, then file the finding referencing the earlier evidence/step id. Only pass wait_until_gone genuine progress/spinner text like "Creating...", "Loading", etc.
  - _evidence:_ On the Procedures 'New Procedure' form, after the real loading text 'Creating...' had already cleared and the error toast 'Missing or insufficient permissions.' was showing, I mistakenly called wait_until_gone(text='Strategic botulinum toxin injection to elevate and shape the eyebrows, creating a more open and youthful eye area') — a static auto-filled procedure description, not a loading indicator. It timed out (never disappears). Subsequent record_finding calls were refused with 'The last screen you read still showed [that text]... the request had not finished' even immediately after a fresh read_screen showing the settled error state. Only worked after navigating to a different screen (Cancel back to the Procedures list) where that string was no longer present in the dump.
- **web-modal-dialog-missing-from-dump** (seen once) — On this web harness, a JS-rendered modal/dialog (e.g. a date-picker 'Go to Date' popup) can be fully visible in a screenshot — with its own title, dropdowns and buttons — while read_screen's dump entirely omits its text and controls, showing only the page underneath. This is unlike the iframe-ownership warning (which does fire correctly for genuinely cross-origin content) — here there is no ownership warning at all, the dump is just silently incomplete. If a screenshot shows an overlay/modal that read_screen's text and touchable-elements list don't mention, don't conclude the modal is absent; screenshot first and drive it via tap_xy with coordinates read off the image (remember the screenshot's pixel size is 2x the logical viewport reported by read_screen, so divide screenshot-image coordinates by 2 before calling tap_xy/type_text).
  - _evidence:_ Calendar module: tapping 'Jump to date' opened a 'Go to Date' modal clearly visible in screenshots (title, month/year dropdowns, day grid, Cancel/Apply buttons), but read_screen's text and touchable-element list right after the tap were identical to the underlying Month-view calendar page with zero mention of the modal — had to locate and click Apply/day-cells purely from screenshot pixel coordinates via tap_xy.
